member: Dalia - Cooperative Use and Produce Preservation Specialist
message:
Amara, Baraka and Chidi, the door stays closed except for quick loading to keep warm air out.

Plainly sorting happens outside and the door opens briefly for one or two crates then shuts, so leakage stays small. The opening is the 800 millimetre hinged door with double gaskets in the seal detail sketch (E59), house door scale passing a 600 by 400 millimetre crate in the stacking crate (E36), with oldest stock sold first, First-In First-Out (FIFO) means oldest sold first, following sorting to remove defects in the postharvest practices (E46).

Amara, Baraka and Chidi, crates stay on shelves behind a lip so cooperative hands lift safely.

Plainly a low rail stops sliding into the aisle during daily checks. The rail is 50 millimetres above each shelf holding 20 kilogramme ventilated crates in the seal detail sketch (E59), luggage scale per lift, and spread floor load of 2.04 kilopascals in the floor pressure calculation (E43) is about one tenth of a person standing so ordinary spreaders carry the tonne.

Amara, Baraka and Chidi, washing stays food safe with one crate moved at a time.

Plainly vented crates wash down and water leaves through the floor drain, keeping high humidity without standing water. I am not ready, because the blocking energy mismatch objection (O1) on peak cooling and wiring with Amara and Baraka is outside my use ownership and must be agreed before a vote.
